verdict.rationale: Warp ships a built-in agent that plans and executes multi-step tasks, runs shell commands and drives interactive programs. Its docs state that you approve actions and review diffs before anything lands, and agent profiles and admin settings control command execution and autonomy. Community users corroborate hands-on delegation, though one Pro user reports agents randomly stopping. Missing for 10: in-depth documentation of the plan-review and per-command approval workflow, and stronger independent corroboration of approval-gated execution reliability.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate terminal tasks to a built-in AI agent that plans and executes commands with my approval

citations.quote: let Warp's built‑in agent handle the rest — writing code, running commands, and iterating until the task is done.
The agent runs shell commands, reads live output, and drives interactive programs like REPLs, database shells, and full-screen apps.
You stay in the loop, approving actions and reviewing diffs before anything lands.
You can prompt the agent in natural language, review and approve its actions, and run shell commands in the same input
Create profiles in the Warp app to configure file access, command execution, MCP server usage, model selection, and directory permissions
